resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. writing §8 line 86: harm: The judge's facts check out, but the harm is thin. I recommend refuting.

What I verified:
- L86 reads `## Phase 5: Close, name the rescue`. Antti authored it on 2026-08-19 (commit 00cf8da7d), and it has not changed since.
- 'rescue' appears at L114, L151, L162 and L163 of the exercise, all below the maintainer cut at L104. The header at L86 is the only student-facing use.
- In output-quality.md the word appears only at L86 and L122-124, below the `<!-- maintainer -->` marker at L75.
- The Phase 5 body (L88-94) never uses the word.

Why it still fails the harm lens:
- (a) Who is worse off? §8 targets private jargon the reader cannot parse, such as self-compound or substrate. 'Rescue' is an ordinary English word. A student reads 'name the rescue' as 'say what the judge saved' and then meets a body that asks whether the judge caught the line they doubted. No one is blocked or misled in the room. The 'mood advertised rather than lived' claim is the maintainer's taste, not a student harm.
- (b) The finding mostly restates the §8 grep test ('can you point to an earning moment?'). It does not describe a consequence.
- (c) The fix has a cost. It changes a student-facing header, so it needs a card. The same file's L66 header, 'Read the scoreboard and name the surprise', carries the same 'name' verb. Fixing only L86 leaves that header in the old style, so the file would be inconsistent. The `phase-5-close-name-the-rescue` anchor is also cited in the language reports and eval body-views. The rename touches more than one line.
- Judge history: all seven judges, including writing, passed this file at the 2026-08-25 audit, with the header unchanged. The 2026-11-14 body rewrite did not touch the header either.
- (d) The 'name' smell in headings (check_student_facing, 2026-08-14) is a different rule from the one filed. It is a real nit that belongs in a sweep covering both L66 and L86. It is not a BLOCKING §8 finding.

Residual: the header slightly presupposes a rescue. The new body says 'you decide whether the doubt was right', so the doubt may turn out wrong. That is a polish issue for a maintainer pass.
